input.quote: Licenses. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, RevMed hereby grants to Sanofi an exclusive (even as to RevMed and its Affiliates), royalty-bearing license (which shall be sub-licensable solely as provided in Section 3.4) under the RevMed Licensed Technology, to Research, Develop, Manufacture, use, sell, offer for sale, import and otherwise Commercialize and exploit Products (including, for clarity, any Companion Diagnostics with respect to such Products) in the Field in the Licensed Territory.
input.rationale: The grant in Section 3.1(a) meets the preferred position. (i) Affiliates and contractors: Section 3.4(a) lets Sanofi exercise its rights and perform its obligations "by itself or through the engagement of any of its Affiliates without RevMed's consent," and Section 3.4(c)(i) lets Sanofi "subcontract to Third Parties the performance of Sanofi's tasks and obligations ... as Sanofi deems appropriate"; sublicensing under Section 3.4(b) is available through multiple tiers, with consent required only for sublicensing substantially all US rights and then "not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned." (ii) Not revocable at will: the licence is not styled revocable, RevMed's termination rights (Sections 12.2(b)-(e)) require uncured material breach, insolvency, a competing product or an uncured diligence failure, and on expiry the Section 3.1 licences "become fully paid up, royalty free, perpetual and irrevocable" (Section 12.3(b)). (iii) Successor transfer: Section 15.2(a)(ii) permits Sanofi to assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or a merger/acquisition, and the Agreement binds successors and permitted assigns. Minor note only: Affiliates take rights through the exercise/assignment mechanics rather than as named direct licensees, and the sublicence grant back to RevMed in Section 3.2 is appropriately limited to performing its obligations — neither point is material, so no redline is warranted.
